bylaw.title: Squamish-Lillooet Regional District Electoral Area D Firearms Bylaw No. 1294-2013

definitions.meaning: shall have the same meaning as in the Firearms Act (British Columbia) Chapter 145 R.S.B.C and Amendments
definitions.quote: “Chief Provincial Firearms Officer” shall have the same meaning as in the Firearms Act (British Columbia) Chapter 145 R.S.B.C and Amendments.

definitions.meaning: shall have the same meaning as in the Firearms Act (British Columbia) Chapter 145 R.S.B.C and Amendments
definitions.quote: “Firearm” or “Firearms” shall have the same meaning as in the Firearms Act (British Columbia) Chapter 145 R.S.B.C and Amendments.

definitions.meaning: shall have the same meaning as in the Firearms Act (British Columbia) Chapter 145 R.S.B.C and Amendments
definitions.quote: “Permit” shall have the same meaning as in the Firearms Act (British Columbia) Chapter 145 R.S.B.C and Amendments.

prohibitions.where: within the limits of the areas defined in Schedules A, and B attached to and forming part of this bylaw
prohibitions.quote: No person may: (a) discharge a firearm within the limits of the areas defined in Schedules A, and B attached to and forming part of this bylaw

prohibitions.what: discharge a firearm on or across a highway or within 100 meters of any school building, school yard, public park, playground, church, cemetery, workshop, place of business, dwelling house, or other place where persons may be assembled or engage in work of any kind
prohibitions.where: on or across a highway or within 100 meters of any school building, school yard, public park, playground, church, cemetery, workshop, place of business, dwelling house, or other place where persons may be assembled or engage in work of any kind
prohibitions.quote: (b) without limiting the foregoing, discharge a firearm on or across a highway or within 100 meters of any school building, school yard, public park, playground, church, cemetery, workshop, place of business, dwelling house, or other place where persons may be assembled or engage in work of any kind.

exceptions.quote: Section 3 of this bylaw does not apply to a person: (a) who is: (i) a peace officer, (ii) a conservation officer, as defined in section 1(1) of the Environmental Management Act (British Columbia), and appointed under the Firearm Act (British Columbia) or the Wildlife Act (British Columbia), (iii) a fisheries officer appointed or designated under the Fisheries Act (Canada), (iv) an officer of the Parks Branch of the Ministry of Environment (British Columbia), (v) in possession of a firearm for use in connection with his or her employment by an armoured car service as defined in the Private Investigators and Security Agencies Act (British Columbia), or (vi) otherwise authorized by any provincial or federal enactment to possess and to discharge a firearm in the performance of his or her duties, when engaged in his or her official duties;

exceptions.permit: a permit issued by the Chief Provincial Firearms Officer to discharge a firearm in an indoor shooting range under the Firearms Act (British Columbia)
exceptions.quote: (b) who is authorized by a permit issued by the Chief Provincial Firearms Officer to discharge a firearm in an indoor shooting range under the Firearms Act (British Columbia);

exceptions.permit: a shooting range approved in writing by the Chief Provincial Firearms Officer
exceptions.quote: (c) who is on a shooting range approved in writing by the Chief Provincial Firearms Officer.

(d) who is a bonafide farmer or their agent acting on behalf of the farmer in rural zoned properties when engaged in a farm operation and the firearm is discharged for the purpose of protecting his or her crops or livestock from birds or animals, or for the purpose of slaughtering livestock on his or her own property, subject to the provisions of the Wildlife Act (British Columbia), Farm Protection Act (British Columbia), and the Livestock Act (British Columbia).

exceptions.applies_to: a closed area (operation of a rifle range or trap club, or both)
exceptions.permit: permission granted by the Regional Board by resolution, on receipt of a written application from an approved club or organization, provided that permission is first received from the local detachment of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, and from the officer named in Section 4.1(c) of this bylaw, as required
exceptions.quote: The Regional Board may by resolution, on receipt of a written application from an approved club or organization, grant permission to the applicant for the operation of a rifle range or trap club, or both, within a closed area, provided that permission is first received from the local detachment of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, and from the officer named in Section 4.1(c) of this bylaw, as required.

distance_rules.from_what: any school building, school yard, public park, playground, church, cemetery, workshop, place of business, dwelling house, or other place where persons may be assembled or engage in work of any kind
distance_rules.quote: within 100 meters of any school building, school yard, public park, playground, church, cemetery, workshop, place of business, dwelling house, or other place where persons may be assembled or engage in work of any kind.

quotes.quote: This bylaw may be cited for all purposes as the ‘Squamish-Lillooet Regional District Electoral Area D Firearms Bylaw No. 1294-2013.’
1317-2014 Amended Sec. 8.1 to include firearm penalties in Area D January 27, 2014
This bylaw applies to those regions in Electoral Area D of the Squamish-Lillooet Regional District as shown on Schedules A, and B, which are attached to and form part of this bylaw.
